text.p: Lithuania received $120 million in new foreign direct investments in the first quarter of 1997, the Lithuanian Investment Agency said on Friday.
"Based on preliminary data from the Lithuanian Statistics Department, the country saw $120 million in new investment during the first quarter of 1997," the Investment Agency said in a statement.
In 1996, $220 million worth of new foreign direct investments flowed into Lithuania, compared to a dismal $49 million in 1995.
At the end of 1996 cumulative direct foreign investment totalled $570 million, the agency said.
"The increases that began in the second half of 1996 and continued in 1997 were more than double most forecasts," the agency added.
